methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 8 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $3.2B - $39.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Applied Intuition, a Series F AI & Software company founded by Qasar Younis and Peter Ludwig, is evaluated against a comp universe of 8 private peers and 1 public reference (Palantir). The private peer set spans similar valuation tier and sector positioning, with valuations ranging from $3.2B to $39.0B.

A stage-progression method was not applicable due to data integrity concerns: the stated last post-money valuation of $15.0B implied a step-up to $19.5B, which exceeds 20x the company's $600M+ total raised and suggests a likely data parsing error. A peer-median approach was therefore the primary triangulation method. The median valuation across the 8-peer AI & Software cohort is $12.0B, with named comparables including Figure AI ($39.0B Series C), Scale AI ($29.0B Private), Reflection AI ($25.0B Series A), Skild AI ($14.0B Series C), and Crusoe Energy ($10.0B Series C).

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $10.2B to $13.8B, with a median point estimate of $12.0B. This represents a discount to the target's stated $15.0B valuation. Key uncertainties include the reliability of the last post-money figure and variation in peer stage advancement and funding efficiency. The compressed peer sample and wide comp range ($3.2B–$39.0B) underscore model sensitivity to peer selection and stage-adjusted growth assumptions.
